about: Attorney Jed Kurzban is an equity partner at Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli and Pratt P.A. in Coral Gables, Florida. Mr. Kurzban focuses his practice on medical malpractice and personal injury matters, representing clients throughout the Coral Gables area.

Mr. Kurzban has been practicing law for over 20 years. An experienced litigator and negotiator, he has fought for and won considerable recoveries on behalf of Florida residents injured due to negligence. He provides committed and personalized service and is dedicated to helping his clients attain all available compensation.

Honoring his accomplishments, the American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys included Mr. Kurzban on its “10 best” list. He is listed in Strathmore’s Who’s Who and holds an AV Preeminent* peer review rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest available rating.
If you haven't already, make sure to check out our Partner Jed Kurzban 's new book How Justice is Served, a #NationalBestseller available here on amazon: https://amzn.to/3nVGm8Q

Over the course of his career, Mr. Kurzban has held many leadership positions in the legal community. He is a former vice-chair of the Dade County Bar Association’s trial section and sat on the board of directors of the Florida Justice Association. He continues to be an active member of both organizations, as well as the Florida Bar, the American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice and the American Constitution Society.

Mr. Kurzban graduated from the University of Alabama with a bachelor’s degree. He earned his law degree from the University of Miami School of Law. He holds a license to practice law in Florida and Hawaii, as well as before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.
